title: Decoding LLM Alignment: A Concise Guide for  GRPO and its variants
gist: A community explainer comparing six RL post-training algorithms for LLMs (PPO, RLOO, GRPO, Pref-GRPO, GSPO, GDPO), arguing the field moved from actor-critic setups to group-normalized and sequence-level optimization, with each method fixing a specific failure of its predecessor.

insights.claim: RL for LLMs has shifted away from complex actor-critic setups toward group-normalized and sequence-level optimization algorithms.
insights.speaker: Sneha Rudra
insights.so_what: Algorithm choice in post-training is trending to critic-free methods that cut memory and compute.

insights.claim: PPO uses a critic network giving a per-token value estimate with clipped policy gradients, suits token-level precision and human preference pairs, but requires memory and compute for the critic.
insights.speaker: Sneha Rudra
insights.so_what: PPO remains the classic RLHF standard but is costly.

insights.claim: RLOO drops the critic and uses the average reward of other completions in a rollout group as the baseline, addressing the hardware overhead of keeping a critic in memory.
insights.speaker: Sneha Rudra
insights.so_what: The efficiency pivot that moved the industry off heavy critic setups.

insights.claim: GRPO samples multiple completions per prompt and computes each advantage by subtracting the group mean reward, which suits math and coding models with automated verifiers and is described as the core engine behind reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1.
insights.speaker: Sneha Rudra
insights.so_what: GRPO with verifiable rewards underlies the reasoning-model wave; verifier-friendly domains are where it applies.
insights.quote: Unlocked the reasoning era - core engine behind reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1

insights.claim: Pref-GRPO uses pairwise win rate within a group instead of raw scores as the reward signal, because scalar rewards are easily gamed when group scores are nearly identical, and suits alignment with subjective multi-criteria preference data.
insights.speaker: Sneha Rudra
insights.so_what: Brings human-preference signal into GRPO without a separate critic or verifier.

insights.claim: GSPO moves ratios and clipping from the token level to the full-sequence level to avoid noisy high-variance gradients and training crashes when training MoE models for reasoning, and is said to enable long-horizon reasoning for large sparse MoE models.
insights.speaker: Sneha Rudra
insights.so_what: Sequence-level optimization is the stability fix for large sparse MoE training; relevant to MoE-based frontier labs.

insights.claim: GDPO normalizes each reward goal independently before adding them, because reward signals collapse when competing goals such as accuracy, safety and brevity are summed, and is said to enable multi-objective alignment.
insights.speaker: Sneha Rudra
insights.so_what: Multi-objective alignment is handled by decoupling reward normalization.

insights.claim: Choosing the right RL method depends on understanding how each constructs its learning signal as RL for language models moves beyond a single reward and a single training recipe.
insights.speaker: Sneha Rudra
insights.so_what: Training-recipe knowledge is differentiating for post-training teams.
